correctness.rationale: For the explicitly listed cubic Desargues graph, a complete independent 2^20-state C++ majority iteration yields 124 fixed points, 7626 primitive two-cycles and the nine claimed basin-size counts; a separate Python enumeration of 2^10 Petersen states and a verified layer-permutation reconstruct the same values through exact phase-preimage products. The equality T(x,y)=(f(y),f(x)) implies exhaustive basin convolution, and base f^6=f^4 gives all five entry-time layers by cumulative squares. All basin weighted counts sum to 1048576, the entry counts sum to the same number, and depth four occurs. No finite simulation is extrapolated to unbounded graph sizes.

value.rationale: The Desargues graph is a standard distance-transitive 20-vertex cubic graph with a Petersen double-cover structure. Knowing 124 fixed states and the previously implied number of two-cycles does not determine the dramatically uneven individual basin populations. The exact full spectrum ranges from singleton basins to a 102152-state anti-consensus oscillation basin, equal to both unanimous basins together, and provides a sharp complete first-entry census. This is a natural complete finite invariant, not a handpicked subcase or trivial restatement of the general bipartite counting lemma.
